name: 45-degree back extension
cue: Hinge at your hips, then squeeze your glutes to a straight line.
research: 45-degree back extension (hyperextension station) done as a hip hinge. The legs lie on the 45-degree line (body 45 deg from vertical at the top): the fronts of the thighs on the hip pad, its upper edge 0.07 H (12 cm) below the hip joint so the pelvis turns freely over it, knees 3 deg, the backs of the ankles under the roller, the soles flat on a foot plate set near perpendicular to the legs (ankle 5 deg). Spine neutral (lumbar and thorax flex 0, spinal flexion 0 throughout): the pelvis and trunk turn as one about the hip axis, hip flexion 75 at the stretch (trunk 120 deg from vertical, the head low in front of the pad) -> 0 at the top, where the body is one straight 45-degree line; the lower back never arches past it (the listed form error). Arms crossed on the chest, each fist on the front of the opposite shoulder. Sources: Jeff Nippard ranks the 45-degree back extension S tier for the glutes (the whole glute works both lengthened at the bottom and shortened at the top); Andersen et al. 2021 (J Sports Sci Med 20:181-187): the 45-degree Roman chair back extension (straight back, from upright down to a ~90 deg hip angle and back) activated the gluteus maximus as much as the Romanian deadlift and the biceps femoris 71-174 % more than the RDL and the seated back-extension machine, with similar erector spinae activity; ExRx (45-degree hyperextension with a straight back: a hip extension, the erector spinae holding the spine as stabilisers). The bottom is set at 75 deg of hip flexion (task band 60-80; Andersen used ~90), about where straight-knee hamstring length stops a neutral spine. Machine: an inclined main beam under the legs on a front post and a rear post, the pad on its upper end, the foot plate on its lower end, the roller on two side posts reaching around the feet; bodyweight (plates held to the chest add load). Primary: gluteus maximus and the hamstrings; secondary: the erector spinae (label Lower back). Geometry: tools/design/back_extension.mjs.

targets.note: trunk_flexion is the thorax tilt from vertical (45 + hip flexion: the body leans 45 deg on the bench); spinal_flexion 0 throughout is the neutral spine, so the top is a straight line with no lumbar hyperextension.

camera.note: Research view: the right profile (az 90, el 5), square to the sagittal plane of the hip hinge. On the 45-degree bench the back of the body faces up and back, so the view turns 20 deg toward the rear and rises 20 deg (az 110, el 25: 28.3 deg in all): the glutes and hamstrings face the camera at the stretch and at the top (phone stage glow about 3600 CSS px at the stretch, 3800 at the top), the amber lower back runs up the spine, and the hinge still reads side-on (the trunk swings from below the horizontal to the 45-degree line). The frame stays under the legs and the hip pad under the thighs, so no machine part crosses the working muscles; the rear foot is short so the base stays clear of the exercise name.
